best_for: Students, teachers and space fans who want to fly between planets, moons and nearby stars in real time on an ordinary PC or Mac, at no cost.
description:
Celestia is a space simulator that draws the universe in 3D as you move through it, from the Celestia Development Team, whose copyright runs from 2001. It opens with Earth in front of a field of stars, and the screen shows your target, your speed and the time in Universal Time.

Roll the mouse wheel to back away light years from Earth, then roll it the other way to come home. You can look up a star by its common name, its Bayer designation or its number in the HIP, HD or SAO catalogs. The solar system browser lists the planets, moons and spacecraft near you, and you can change how the program starts by editing a plain-text start.cel file. A user's guide by Frank Gregorio is available in several languages.

points.title: Fly anywhere, at any date
points.text: You pick an object and press G to travel there, then orbit with the mouse. A tour guide lists interesting stops, and a star browser shows the 100 nearest or brightest stars from where you are.

points.title: Free under the GPL
points.text: Celestia is open-source software under GPL 2.0 or later, made by a volunteer team. There is nothing to buy and no account.

points.title: Add your own worlds
points.text: Real, hypothetical or fictional objects go in as plain-text catalog files for solar systems, stars and deep-sky objects, dropped into the extras folder without touching the built-in data.

points.title: Development is slow
points.text: The newest stable release, 1.6.4, came out in November 2023 and mainly fixed the site address and Lua 5.4 builds. Expect few updates.

points.title: Small version history
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 3 versions, as a 32-bit installer for all users. macOS has one universal zip. There is no Linux build here, though the project publishes a source tarball.
